# R3 — Stop silently skipping child audits on wall-clock exhaustion; right-size budgets

**Parent:** SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL (RCA: audit Phase 1/Phase 2 reliability)
**Discovered-from:** SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 (audit, 2026-09-15).

## Problem

Wall-clock/budget exhaustion is the **dominant genuine failure mode**, not JSON
parsing. Stored audit reports (2026-09-15 export) contain:

- `Skipped due to audit timeout. Manual audit required` ~176.
- `Audit runner skipped this child after Ns total elapsed time to avoid the
  parent process timeout` ~100+ (observed parent budgets vary widely:
  ~120s, 900s, 1500s, 3110s).
- `Pi model call timed out after 1800s` 16.
- `pending deep code review` 88.

Children are silently skipped when the cumulative elapsed-time guard trips,
forcing a full manual re-audit. Prior art: SA-0MSF4AFXF000M5DN (right-size the
parent-timeout guard), SA-0MSABZO2T004B95X (configurable cumulative guard),
SA-0MS0SQQTW006GNX9 / SA-0MS3FNIUA00385DE / SA-0MQPQX57I0055ITT (Phase 2
timeouts).

## Desired change

Derive parent-process and per-call budgets from measured per-call timing
(already emitted as `Per-call timing:` lines) with an explicit margin; and when
a budget is exhausted, record an explicit `partial (budget exceeded)` result
plus a resumable checkpoint instead of a bare skip.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A documented budget baseline (p50/p95 per phase from `Per-call timing`
   lines) underpins the parent-process and per-call budgets; the previously
   inconsistent observed values (~120s/900s/1500s/3110s) are replaced by a
   single right-sized value (or documented derivation).
2. When the budget is exhausted, the affected child/AC is recorded
   `partial (budget exceeded)` with a clear diagnostic naming the budget and
   the remediation (`--parent-timeout` / `AUDIT_PARENT_TIMEOUT`), never a bare
   skip that hides the cause.
3. A resumed run reuses the phase checkpoint (SA-0MT6EZUS9004FJ9T) and
   completes the previously skipped children without re-running completed
   phases.
4. Regression test: simulate budget exhaustion -> child recorded explicitly,
   checkpoint written, resume completes the child.
5. `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` documents the budget model and the
   budget-exceeded contract.
6. Full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- UK English.
- Must not weaken the fail-closed behaviour: an unverified AC never becomes
  `met`.
- Keep resume idempotent and HEAD-keyed (do not reuse stale checkpoints).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MSL6DQVN0036IGM** – Verification: monitored-run guidance tests (completed)
- **SA-0MTHC710X003ORZM** – Audit staleness race: post-persist comment bumps updatedAt past auditedAt — passed audits show stale icon (completed)
- **SA-0MS9B91Q5002AXZ3** – Fix implement.py sys.path resolution when skills dir is a symlink (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 0mt6ezus9004fj9t, 120s, 1800s, acceptance, affected (+116 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0mt6ezus9004fj9t, 1800s, acceptance, affected, already (+111 more)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: 0mt6ezus9004fj9t, 1800s, acceptance, already, art (+101 more)

# R4 — Prevent concurrency saturation from aborting the Phase 1 parent screen

## Problem statement

Host-wide audit concurrency saturation can abort the Phase 1 parent screen
before any Pi call is made, even when the audit's work item itself is the
highest-value call in the pipeline. In the motivating audit (SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0)
the Phase 1 parent screen waited 90 s, found no semaphore slot (all held by
concurrent audits), and returned `unmet` for every AC with a bare
`queue saturated` message — zero Pi calls were made at all.

Stored reports contain ~12 occurrences of `Audit concurrency limit reached`.

## Users

- **Release operator** running an automated audit of a work item: the audit must
  complete its highest-value Phase 1 parent screen so the work item can be
  assessed for release readiness.
- **Producer** reviewing audit results: a `unmet` verdict caused by infrastructure
  saturation is misleading and wastes time.
- **Agent** running audits concurrently: needs predictable, fair access to the
  semaphore without being starved by lower-priority calls.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Strict priority for Phase 1 parent screening.** When `_acquire_audit_slot`
   is called for a Phase 1 parent context (`context="parent"`), the ticket is
   enqueued at `Priority.CRITICAL` regardless of the work item's own priority.
   A CRITICAL ticket is always dequeued before any MEDIUM or LOW ticket, so
   lower-priority concurrent calls cannot starve the parent screen.

2. **Actionable failure mode.** When no slot is available within the bounded
   wait, the error message/report includes:
   - The current queue depth (number of items waiting)
   - The elapsed wait time
   - An explicit retry action (e.g. "retry in X seconds after fewer audits complete")
   Not a bare `queue saturated` with no next step.

3. **Concurrency test passes.** A test that launches >= 2 simultaneous audits
   (each with a Phase 1 parent screen) shows the first audit's Phase 1 parent
   screen **completing** (it may wait in the queue) rather than returning
   `unmet` with zero Pi calls. The audit may time out overall but must not
   fail-fast at the semaphore acquisition step.

4. **Queue wait time observable.** Per-call timing output (stderr line or report
   field) includes the time spent waiting in the admission queue, so operators
   can measure contention without a debug log.

5. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- UK English.
- Do not remove the host-wide concurrency cap; bound the wait and prioritise correctly.
- Changes must be backward-compatible: existing callers that pass their own
  priority value continue to work as before; the Phase 1 parent call site
  is the only one that needs the CRITICAL override.
- The priority queue depth (default 50) and queue timeout (default 90 s) are
  sufficient for normal operation; do not change these defaults.

## Existing state

- `_acquire_audit_slot()` in `audit_runner.py` already implements a bounded
  priority-queue admission protocol (SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM).
- `_call_pi()` wraps every Pi subprocess launch inside `_acquire_audit_slot`.
- `_call_phase1_screen()` accepts a `priority` parameter and forwards it to
  `_call_pi` → `_call_pi_and_maybe_log` → `_call_pi`.
- `_phase1_parent_screening()` calls `_call_phase1_screen` with
  `priority=_resolve_audit_priority(ctx.work_item)` — this maps the work
  item's WL priority to a queue priority, which is **MEDIUM** by default.
- The semaphore has `max_workers=2` (default, configurable via `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY`).
- The queue has `max_depth=50` (default).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
  - `_acquire_audit_slot()` — enqueue priority for parent calls
  - `_phase1_parent_screening()` — pass CRITICAL priority for parent context
  - `_call_phase1_screen()` — accept priority=None → CRITICAL for parent
  - Error message format in `TimeoutError` raised by `_acquire_audit_slot`
  - `_log_audit_slot()` — add queue-depth to the timing line

- `skill/shared/queue.py`
  - `PriorityQueue.peek()` / `PriorityQueue.rank()` — expose queue depth in error

- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py`
  - `Semaphore.acquire()` — expose slot count in TimeoutError message

- `tests/test_audit_runner.py` or new test file
  - Concurrency saturation test with 2+ simultaneous audits

## Related work

- **SA-0MSGEAZMC009LHKL** — fail immediately on audit concurrency limit (prior art, superseded by queue admission)
- **SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM** — integrate bounded priority queue (replaces fail-fast)
- **SA-0MSAK2SNN005HCM5** — audit runner concurrency cap
- **SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL** — parent RCA item (discovery source, F4 finding)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** The Phase 1 parent screen is the highest-value call in the
  pipeline and should always be admitted first. Child screens and Phase 2 calls
  can wait longer.
- **Risk:** Forcing CRITICAL priority on ALL parent calls could mean a
  non-critical work item's parent screen jumps ahead of a critical work item's
  child deep analysis. Mitigation: the queue is per-work-item in practice
  (each audit is a separate process), so contention is between independent
  audits, not within a single audit.
- **Risk:** Changing the error message format may break automated parsers that
  look for the exact `queue saturated` string. Mitigation: keep the original
  substring in the new message for backward compatibility.
- **Risk:** The concurrency test requires orchestrating multiple concurrent
  audit processes. Mitigation: use a mock Semaphore to simulate saturation
  without requiring real concurrent processes.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Should the Phase 1 parent screen always get CRITICAL priority, or only
  when the work item itself is marked critical/high? — **Decision:** Always
  CRITICAL. The parent screen is the highest-value call in the audit pipeline;
  child screens and Phase 2 calls are secondary and can wait.
- Q: What should the error message include for AC2? — **Decision:** Queue
  depth (from `len(queue)`), elapsed wait time (from `time.monotonic()`), and
  an explicit retry action ("retry in N seconds").
- Q: How should the concurrency test simulate saturation? — **Decision:** Mock
  the Semaphore to hold all slots permanently for N seconds, then release them,
  so the test verifies that a Phase 1 parent call waits (does not fail-fast).
data.title: R4: Prevent concurrency saturation from aborting the Phase 1 parent screen

# Resume completion for budget-exceeded children

## Summary
A resumed run detects budget-exceeded children in the checkpoint and re-audits them without re-running completed phases.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. On resume, budget-exceeded children (marked with budget-exceeded diagnostic) are identified and re-audited.
2. Completed phases from the prior run are skipped.
3. Budget-exceeded children complete successfully without re-running completed parent phases.

## Implementation Notes
- Update checkpoint store to track per-child budget-exceeded status.
- On resume (checkpoint.is_resuming == True), identify children marked as budget-exceeded.
- Re-run Phase 1/2 for those children only, skipping already-completed phases.
- The resume logic should distinguish between:
  - children skipped due to budget exhaustion (re-audit)
  - children completed in prior run (skip)
  - children that never started (normal processing)
- See SA-0MT6EZUS9004FJ9T for checkpoint resume architecture.

## Key Files:
- skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py
- skill/audit/scripts/checkpoint_store.py

## Planning Complete — auto-plan (effort/risk below threshold)

**Pre-check:** `plan-if-needed` → `decision: skip` (effort **Extra Small**, risk **Low**). Approval gate → `request_approval: false` (Extra Small + Low). No decomposition required; the six review stages were run against the existing content.

### Review stage summary

1. **Requirements & AC alignment** — The three user stories (release operator, producer, concurrent agent) map cleanly onto the ACs: AC1 (CRITICAL priority for the Phase 1 parent ticket) covers the operator/agent starvation story; AC2 (actionable failure mode) covers the producer's misleading-verdict story; AC3/AC4 cover verification and observability; AC5 covers regression safety. Every AC traces back to a stated requirement; no missing, contradictory, or invented ACs. No change made.
2. **Completeness** — Required fields (description, ACs) present, as are constraints, existing state, related work, risks and the Q&A appendix. `validate_key_files_format()` and `validate_key_files_in_description()` both return zero issues, and every predicted file/symbol was verified present: `_acquire_audit_slot()` (audit_runner.py L2411), `_phase1_parent_screening()` (L8556), `_call_phase1_screen()` (L8318, already accepts `priority: int | None = None`), `_log_audit_slot()` (L2390), `PriorityQueue.peek()`/`rank()` (skill/shared/queue.py L471/523), `Semaphore.acquire()` (skill/shared/process_semaphore.py L160). No change made.
3. **Sequencing & dependencies** — No children exist and `wl dep list` shows no inbound/outbound edges. The only upstream prerequisite (SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM, bounded priority-queue admission) is already **completed**, so no blocking edge is needed. AC ordering is coherent: AC1/AC2 are the code change, AC3 the test, AC5 the full-suite gate. No change made.
4. **Scope sizing** — No children; the item is a single Extra Small fix in one function plus its error message. Decomposition would create artificial overhead, so no child items were created (documented decision). No-op.
5. **Acceptance & testability** — AC1–AC5 are all binary pass/fail and testable. Two accuracy notes (no intent change): AC4's artefact already exists — `_log_audit_slot()` emits `wait_seconds` derived from `time.time()`, so the AC is verifiable as written; AC2 is partially satisfied by the existing message (`Audit concurrency limit reached: {exc}. Retry when fewer audits are running.`), leaving **queue depth** as the main outstanding element. No change made.
6. **Polish & handoff** — Description is well structured, UK English, and directly actionable (problem, users, ACs, constraints, existing state, key files, related work, risks). No change made.

**AC coverage review** (`run_coverage_review`): `recommendation: proceed` — fully covered, `coverage_pct: 100.0`, no unresolved conflicts. No gaps needed auto-closing.

### Vertical-slice decision

The item is small enough that phasing is not required (recorded per the plan skill's step 5). The implementer delivers one vertical slice: priority override at the parent call site + enriched `TimeoutError`/verdict message + queue-wait observability + a concurrency-saturation test + full-suite verification.

### Observations recorded (no intent change applied)

- **Claim-guard defect encountered this session (not an Open Question for this item).** `StatusLifecycle.require_claimed()` compares the live status against the literal `"in_progress"` while the `wl` CLI stores/reports `"in-progress"` (hyphenated), so the guard fails closed even though the claim is genuinely held. Verified: `wl update … --status in_progress` → `wl show` reports `in-progress`. Already tracked by **SA-0MTYMFLZD004O2VV** and **SA-0MTYMCWYW004KV6G**; no new work item created. This plan session therefore asserted the claim directly via `wl show` (`status: in-progress`) and released to `open` only at completion.
- **Risk-section nuance.** The "Risks & assumptions" note says to preserve the exact substring `queue saturated`; the current `TimeoutError` text is `audit concurrency queue 'audit' saturated: no slot within 90s`, which does not contain that exact phrase. Implementers should preserve the existing wording (and add the new fields) rather than introducing the literal `queue saturated` where it never appeared. Recorded as guidance only.

### Status transition

Stage advanced to `plan_complete`; status released to `open`. Next step: `/skill:implement SA-0MU32T8SH001R8MZ`.
